To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a retrograde survival signal from distal axons to cell bodies can be carried by a type of signaling endosomes not necessarily transporting NGFs or phosphorylated Trks, and that the retrograde survival signaling pathway can be activated without activation of Trks by neurotrophic ligands.

the retrograde survival signaling of NGF in mammalian neurons is mediated by mechanisms downstream from TrkA and that the retrograde signal can be carried to the cell bodies from the distal axon by a signaling endosome that is not necessarily transporting NGFs or phosphorylated Trks in its lumen.

retrograde NGF survival signals can be blocked by a kinase inhibitor applied only to the distal axon, and that NGF is not required for retrograde survival signaling in the presence of the kinase inhibitor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the retrograde survival signaling mechanism(s) in sympathetic neurons.
the mechanisms by which the retrograde survival signaling system is regulated, and we suggest that retrograde survival signaling may be more complex than currently thought.
the question of whether NGF or its receptor, Trka, are essential for the retrograde survival signaling from NGF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NGF-induced retrograde survival signals are mediated by a combination of TrkA-dependent and -independent downstream signaling pathways.

the NGF-induced retrograde survival signals are carried by mechanisms downstream of the TrkA receptor in the axons, but that the NGF-TrkA interaction is required for the activation of these downstream mechanisms in the axons and for the survival effect of NGF on the neurons.

the retrograde survival signaling from NGF to its cell body is not blocked by local inhibition of Trk phosphorylation in the distal or proximal axons but that the survival signaling can be triggered in the distal and proximal axon segments by NGF-independent mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NGF-induced retrograde survival signals are mediated by downstream signals activated by TrkA phosphorylated by NGF in the distal terminals, but that NGF-independent survival signals can also be activated by alterations in kinase activities in the cell body and distal axons.

NGF-induced TrkA phosphorylating activity in the distal neurites of sympathetic neurons can initiate retrograde signaling to the cell bodies by mechanisms not requiring NGF, phosphorylated Trk, or endocytosis.
the retrograde survival signaling pathway is more complex than the current theory suggests.
The main takeaway from our work is that

retrograde survival signals in sympathetic neurons do not travel from the distal axon terminals in NGF-bound endosomes containing phosphorylated TrkAs in their membranes, but instead arise from downstream kinases in the distal terminals.
the retrograde survival signaling pathway is complex and not as straightforward as the current theory suggests.
retrograde signaling is not necessarily mediated by NGF or TrkA, but can be mediated by downstream signals activated by TrkA.
